proposal.utterance: What BFO category best fits 'the normative force of an obligation'?

entities.label: NormativeForce
entities.rationale: Normative force is the capacity of an obligation to bind, direct, or compel behavior. It is internally grounded in the obligation bearer (the norm-bearing entity or the obligation itself), which makes it a Disposition rather than a Role. It is not a Quality because it is not a static measurable property but rather a potentiality that is realized through compliance or enforcement processes. It is not yet realized until acted upon, fitting BFO_0000016 (Disposition) well.

relations.rationale: NormativeForce is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016): it is an internally grounded realizable entity inhering in a bearer (the obligation-bearing entity) that can be realized in processes of compliance, enforcement, or adjudication.

NormativeForce inheres in instances of LegalObligation; however, since LegalObligation is typed as BFO_0000023 (Role), the relation is better expressed as: NormativeForce instances inhere in (RO_0000052) bearers that are also bearers of LegalObligation. This subClassOf is flagged as an open question.

open_questions: Should NormativeForce inhere in the LegalObligation individual/role itself, or in the person who bears the obligation? BFO requires SDCs to inhere in a single bearer — clarifying the bearer type is needed before committing the inheres-in relation.

Is 'normative force' meant as a general philosophical class (applicable to any obligation, moral or legal) or specifically to legal obligations only? If the former, it should be a broader class; if the latter, it could be constrained to legal contexts.

Could normative force alternatively be modeled as a Quality (BFO_0000019) — a static property of the obligation at a time — rather than a Disposition? This depends on whether you view it as a standing potentiality (Disposition) or a present property (Quality). The distinction matters for how realization is modeled.

The existing class LegalObligation has dual parents BFO_0000023 (Role) and BFO_0000020 (SDC). Should NormativeForce be modeled as a quality or disposition that is part of what makes something a LegalObligation, or as a separate SDC that co-inheres in the same bearer?
proposal.rationale_summary: The question asks for the best BFO category for 'the normative force of an obligation.' Normative force is the capacity or potentiality by which an obligation binds or directs the behavior of its bearer — it is not a static measurable property (ruling out Quality/BFO_0000019) and not an externally-grounded social function (ruling out Role/BFO_0000023). Rather, it is an internally grounded potentiality that can be realized in processes of compliance, enforcement, or adjudication, which maps onto Disposition (BFO_0000016). A new class NormativeForce is proposed as a subclass of BFO_0000016. The direct relation to LegalObligation is flagged as an open question because BFO requires identifying the precise material or social bearer of this disposition, and the existing LegalObligation class has a dual typing (Role + SDC) that needs resolution before the inheres-in relation can be safely committed.
